_note: Our own writing. The tutorial briefing: situation, goal and stakes (Core p.40-43), License Levels (p.18), the Everest (p.31).

open.speaker: npc
line: Listen up, rookies. I'm {npc}, and for the next few hours you belong to me. You're new pilots, License Level zero: everyone starts there. You'll fly the GMS Everest, the standard Union frame, with standard gear.

how.speaker: npc
line: Every mission starts like this: a briefing. I tell you the situation, you figure out the goal, and we both know the stakes. Today's situation: a live-fire range and a pack of training drones.

questions.speaker: npc
line: Anything else before you mount up?

choices.text: Can we get hurt out there?

everest.speaker: npc
line: Because every pilot in Union is licensed for it, from day one. It's tough, it's flexible, and it'll forgive your mistakes. Mostly.

enemy.speaker: npc
line: Training drones. They shoot back, softly. Learn on them, so you don't learn on something real.

die.speaker: npc
line: Not today. Your mech can be wrecked, and the printer will make you a new one. Out there, for real, it's another story.

close.speaker: npc
line: Good. Check your reserves, then deploy. I'll be talking you through it the whole way.
